title: Pediatric arch support: background review
coords: x and y are percent of the page image, measured from the top left
intro: Our seven-page review of flat feet, existing treatments and adjustable-insole requirements.

hotspots.title: The problem
hotspots.note: The review frames the problem as a device for growing children aged 5 to 7. It sets two design targets: up to 10% volumetric foot growth and a 150 N ground-reaction load.

hotspots.title: Typical arch against flat arch
hotspots.note: Figure 1 sets a typical arch beside a flat one: the footprint fills in and the ankle leans. The image is credited to Cleveland Clinic (source 3). We did not draw it.

hotspots.title: Orthotics
hotspots.note: Our background review discusses orthotics for children with symptomatic flat feet. We aimed for an adjustable sleeve.

hotspots.title: What the device must not disturb
hotspots.note: Tables of foot structures and the gait cycle, each with a line on what the device must leave alone. 'Flexible and soft enough to disperse forces' pushed us toward gel and fabric over plastic.

hotspots.title: Orthotics evidence
hotspots.note: Two of the three papers found weak or uneven evidence for orthotics. The 2018 review included 11 of 606 studies; it did not test our sleeve.

hotspots.title: Design requirements
hotspots.note: The review lists concerns about stiffness, muscle use and outgrowing the insole. We used these to draft requirements.

hotspots.title: Patients, providers, payers
hotspots.note: Users sorted into patients, providers and payers: a parent has to put it on a small child, a clinician has to demonstrate it quickly, a payer wants it safe. I coordinated the clinical-contact side.

hotspots.title: Two products already on sale
hotspots.note: We compared two existing products by price, features and fit as the foot grows.

hotspots.title: Our column in the benchmark
hotspots.note: The last column rates our sleeve 'High' for adaptability and comfort. That is design intent from the design review. Neither was measured.

hotspots.title: Sleeve proposal
hotspots.note: We proposed an adjustable sleeve based on the literature and product comparison. Costs and clinical benefit were not tested.
